readings_chosen: Sentence 1: ‘The account says’ can be ignored when summarising informally, but here it explicitly reports inner content. I place opening, dryness and the causal claim in account_world, with no inherited actual premises. There is no inference that the narrator endorses the account.

Sentence 1: ‘caused’ asserts production, so the relation is BECAUSE, not SINCE or SO THAT. It points at opening and dry. The causal assertion supplies no general MAKES rule; writing such a rule would turn the very claim being checked into its own premise.

Sentence 1: ‘opening the window’ has no named actor. I retain it as the Fact ‘window was opened’, rather than invent a person or use a full DOER–VERB–THING happening with an added doer. Open stays open; no release or open-a-fist shape is substituted. Its causal efficacy is asserted only by line because.

Sentence 1: the report’s wording commits that account to an opening and the letter staying dry, as well as their claimed causal relation. Those endpoints are therefore TOLD said-content. Neither the purpose of opening nor a separate change/depends relation is supplied. No body response or opening geometry is guessed.
